input.question: Why doesn't Disney just buy back the rights?
input.ground_truth: Contracts. 20th Century Fox currently has distribution deal for Fantastic Four films, so trying to break that deal might have some negative consequences that Disney might not want to bother with. Also, it's worth pointing out that as far as Marvel's roster of superheroes go, the Fantastic Four are pretty craptastic. The money makers for Marvel have always been heroes like Spider-Man, the Hulk, Iron Man, and Captain America. This is why we're seeing Disney so focused on the Avengers and the heroes that make up the team. Not many people are clamoring to see the Fantastic Four in action (especially after those first two movies), so Disney probably doesn't care enough to make an offer to buy the rights back. Now, if we were talking about someone like Spider-Man, Disney would probably shell out the cash. I just have a hard time imagining that the Fantastic Four is high up on the company's priority list.

response.prediction:
Okay, let’s imagine you have a really cool toy that you once played with, but now someone else is playing with it because they borrowed it from you a long time ago and promised they could play with it for a while. But now, you really want your toy back.

Now, the person who has your toy might not want to give it back right now, or maybe they want to play with it a little longer, or maybe they want you to give them more of your other toys or some money to trade for it.

Disney is like that person who wants their toy (which is like a movie or a story they used to own). But sometimes, the person who has the toy (the rights) doesn’t want to give it back for free, or maybe they want Disney to give them something special in return.

So, Disney can try to "buy back" the rights, but if the other person doesn’t want to sell, or if it costs too many of Disney’s toys (money), then Disney can’t just take the toy back without asking nicely and maybe giving something in return.

That’s why Disney doesn’t always just buy back the rights—they have to talk about it and sometimes pay a lot to get their toy back!
